FRIDAY, MAY 13, 1910
Meeting called to order at 10.15 A. M. at Rosse Hall, Bro. Bridgman in
the Chair.
The minutes of yesterday's meeting were read, corrected and approved.
Committee on Credentials reported that tbe credentials of Thomas Mar
shall UptegrafE {Eta '10) had been accepted.
The Chair stated that the telegrams to the Aztec Club and Bro. Goldwin
Smith had been transmitted (Appendixes D and E).
The Chair suggested an invitation to President Peirce, of Kenyon Col
lege, to address the Convention, which was approved by the delegates. The
hour was set at 3 P. M. Friday.
The Committee to Nominate Members of the Executive Council reported
that Bro. Leo Weldon Wertheimer (Iota '99) and Bro. Albert Draper Whiting
(litit '88) were nominated for the term ending 1915, Moved by Bro. Holton
(Xi '10) and seconded by Bro. Wiedersheim (Tau'lO) that report be adopted.
The report was adopted.

Bro. Wertheimer announced that the Convention picture would be taken
immediately after adjournment.
Bro. Noyes (Chi '10) moved that the Committee on New Bu,siness draw
up a resolution to the effect that each chapter contribute fifty dollars a year

1910, as reported by the Chapters, was 585, an increase of 1 over 1909. A

Second Supplement to Catalogue. In March, 1910, blanks were
forwarded to the Chapters with request to furnish on or before April 9 lists
of the names, symbols and addresses of initiates since February 1, 1908, not
included in the supplemental membership list of 1908. It was expected that
the information would be promptly received and that the pamphlets would
be ready for dist ibution in May. At the meeting of the council held on
April 11, it was reported that ten of the Chapters has not yet sent in their
lists, and the Recorder, in his printed communication of April 13, accompany
ing the printed minutes of the meeting, called special attention to the matter.
At the meeting of the Council on
May 9, five Chapters were reported as stdl
in default. In the opinion of the Council the delay in furnishing the inform �
ation is inexcusable. It is hoped that the delinquent Chapters will take the
matter up immediately.

New Song Book, There are still on hand about 125 copies of the Song
Book. The books are sold at two dollars plus carrying charges.

Fraternity

Archives. Since the last Convention the various books, papers, docu
ments and memorabilia in the custody of the Council have been classified,
arranged and indexed by Brother Fisher, Archivist, and are stored in fire
proof warehouse. We trust that at some time (not too long deferred) suitable
provision may be made for housing the Archives where they may be easily
accessible to all tlie members of the Fraternity. In this conection the Council
would express the wish that the Viirious Chapters and Associations of Alumni
would hereafter, whenever possible, send to the Council duplicate copies of
their programs, menus, souvenirs and memorabilia of their various Fraternity
functions.
Collection of Brother Albert Poole Jacobs. At the last Convention
the Executive Council was authorized to make suitable appropriation for the
purpose of purchasing the collection of the late Brother Albert Poole Jacobs
(Phi '73) relating to Greek Letter fraternities (General Resolution No. 4).
'The collection has been forwarded to the Council and examined, and a pay
ment of five hundred dollars on account has been made. The Council now
recommends the payment of a further and final sum of five hundred dollars,
making one thousand dollars in all.
Inter-Fraternity Conference. At a meeting of the Council held
October 22, 1909, the matter of participating in an informal conference of all
Greek Letter Fraternities, called by President Faunce of Brown University,
to be held in New York City November 27, 1909, was submitted for consider
ation. The Council did not participate in the conference, but decided to sub
mit the whole subject to this Convention. A participation in such general
conference would be something new in our Fraternity life. Whether modern
conditions in the colleges and fraternities render official co-operation in any
form or to any extent necessary or dt sirable is obviously a question of impor
tance. We are advised that very many of the fraternities, including most of
the leading ones, were represented at the informal conference held last year,
and we have been invited to join the conference to be held in 1910. A full
expression of opinion is desired from the Chapters before accepting such in-

13
;vitation. As an indication of the scope of the work proposed by the con ference the Council submits herewith printed matter received under date of
April 15, 1910, from a Committee of "The Inter-Fraternity Conference." *
Aztec Club. The Convention of 1909 adopted a resolution that the
Aztec Club of the University of Illinois be granted a Charter of this Fra
ternity (General Resolution No. 6). The matter was duly submitted to the
Chapters, and on April 26, 1910, the last report was received. All of the
Chapters have voted unanimously in favor of the application except the Iota
Chapter, whose vote was nine (9) in favor to three (3) against. The resolu
tion of 1909 has, therefore, been duly ratified, and the Executive Council is
now charged with the duty of proper installation, pursuant to Article Hi.,
Section 3, of the Constitution.
Cni Delta Psi. The Chi Delta Psi Society of Toronto University,
Canada, has recently announced a desire to renew at the present Convention
its application for a Charter of the Fraternity and to be heard through its
representatives.
Proposed Dinner to Brother Taft. A committee has been appointed
by the Council to wait upon the President, Brother William Howard Taft
Beta '78, and to invite him to attend a Psi Upsilon dinner in New York City
on a date to be selected by him, preferably as near as possible to Founders'
Day, November 24, 1910. In case the dinner is held. Brother John C.
Spooner, of the Rho Chapter, will be invited to act as toastmaster.
The Council. The officers of the Council during the past year have
been : President, Brother Bridgman ; Secretary, Brother Coleman ; Treasurer,
Brother Poole. Brother Shattuck was elected Recorder of the Council in place
of Brother Saxe, who resigned as Recorder on October 22, 1909. Brother Fisher
continued as Archivist, and Brother David Orr (Delta, 1897) was appointed
Assistant Secretary. Seven meetings of the CouLcil have been held during
the year, with an average attendance of eight members, and printed copies of
the minutes of each meeting have been regularly sent to the Chapters.
The terms of Brothers Wertheimer and Whiting expire in 1910, and this
Convention will be called upon to elect two members for the term' expirine
1915.
Treasurer's Report. The report of the Treasurer is submitted here
with.

standing of the Fraternity throughout the country, and the general interest
maintained by the Chapters in their Fraternity and Chapter work. The
single suggestion now offered to the Chapters is the cultivation of the habit
of careful and prompt attention to details of Fraternity business.

To THE Aztec Club,

The Convention learns with pleasure from the Executive Council that the

Fraternity.
